title: Ordering Drinks at a Cafe
summary: Cafes sell many kinds of drinks, from hot coffee to cold fruit teas. Knowing a few simple words helps you order quickly and feel confident.

cover.alt: A cafe counter with a hot latte and a cold iced fruit tea. A barista waits behind the counter.

blocks.title: Drinks at a Cafe
paragraphs: Cafes sell many kinds of drinks, from hot coffee to cold fruit teas. Knowing a few simple words helps you order quickly and feel confident. You will read about popular cafe drinks and common ways to order them, then practise in two short conversations.

items.prompt: Do you like hot drinks or cold drinks?
items.answer: Open answer. For example: I like cold drinks, especially iced tea.
items.explanation: Both hot and cold drinks are popular in cafes.

items.prompt: What drink do you usually order at a cafe?
items.answer: Open answer. For example: I usually order a latte.
items.explanation: A latte is a popular choice at many cafes.

items.prompt: Can you name one drink that does not have coffee in it?
items.answer: Open answer. For example: Green tea, hot chocolate, or lemonade.
items.explanation: Many cafes have lots of options without coffee.

blocks.title: Popular Cafe Drinks
paragraphs: Cafes offer a wide range of drinks. Espresso is a small, strong coffee. A latte mixes espresso with steamed milk and has a mild, creamy taste. A cappuccino is similar but has a thick layer of foam on top.

Not everyone wants coffee. Hot chocolate is sweet and popular in winter. Green tea is a light option with a gentle flavour. Many cafes also sell iced drinks. An iced latte is a latte served over ice. Fruit teas, like peach or mango tea, are sweet and cold. Most cafes let you choose the size: small, medium, or large.

items.prompt: What is the difference between a latte and a cappuccino?
items.answer: A latte has steamed milk and a mild, creamy taste. A cappuccino is similar but has a thick layer of foam on top.
items.explanation:
Both use espresso and milk, but the amount of foam is different.

Which one do you think you would prefer?

rows.term: I would like a latte, please.
rows.meaning: A polite way to order a drink.
rows.example: I would like a latte, please. Medium size.

rows.meaning: The barista asks about the size of your drink.
rows.example: What size would you like? Small, medium, or large?

rows.meaning: You ask for the drink to be served cold over ice.
rows.example: Can I have it iced? It is hot today.

rows.meaning: You ask whether the drink contains milk.
rows.example: Is there milk in this? I prefer no milk.

blocks.title: How to Order at a Cafe
paragraphs: Ordering at a cafe usually follows a simple pattern. First, the barista greets you. You say what you want. The barista may ask about size, milk type, or extras.

For example, at Starbucks you choose a size first: tall (small), grande (medium), or venti (large). At a local cafe, you can just say small, medium, or large. After you order, the barista tells you the price. You pay, then wait for your name to be called or for the barista to bring your drink to the counter.
Most cafes are happy to make small changes to your drink. For example, you can swap regular milk for oat milk, or ask for no sugar. Keep any request short and clear.

items.prompt: What does a barista usually ask after you say what drink you want?
items.answer: The barista usually asks about the size, the type of milk, or any extras you want.
items.explanation:
These questions help the barista make your drink exactly the way you like it.

Can you think of one extra you might want to add to a coffee?

rows.term: Can I have oat milk instead?
rows.meaning: You ask to change the type of milk in your drink.
rows.example: Can I have oat milk instead? I do not drink cow's milk.

rows.meaning: You ask the barista not to add sugar.
rows.example: A green tea, please. No sugar, please.

rows.meaning: The barista asks if you will drink inside or take the drink away.
rows.example: For here or to go? I will drink it here.
How much is that? I have cash.

blocks.title: Scene: Ordering a Hot Drink
paragraphs: You are inside a small, warm cafe on a cool morning. The cafe has a wooden counter and a handwritten menu on the wall. The barista, Sam, is standing behind the counter and smiling.
You want a hot drink. You are not sure about the size, so you plan to ask.
Your goal is to order a hot drink, ask about the size options, and complete your order.

images.alt: A cool morning in a small cafe. A barista stands ready at a wooden counter.

turns.speaker: Barista
turns.text: Good morning! What can I get for you today?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Good morning. I would like a latte, please.

turns.speaker: Barista
turns.text: Of course. What size would you like? Small, medium, or large?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: What is the difference in price?

turns.speaker: Barista
turns.text: Small is the cheapest, and large is the biggest. Most people get medium.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Medium, please. And can I have oat milk instead of regular milk?

turns.speaker: Barista
turns.text: No problem at all. For here or to go?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: For here, please. How much is that?

turns.speaker: Barista
turns.text: That is four fifty. I will call your name when it is ready.

blocks.title: Scene: Ordering a Cold Drink
paragraphs: It is a hot afternoon. You walk into the same cafe and go to the counter. The barista, Sam, is there again. The menu shows several cold drinks, including iced lattes and fruit teas.
You want something cold and fruity, but you are not sure which fruit tea to choose.
Your goal is to ask about the fruit teas, choose one, and order it without sugar.

images.alt: The same cafe on a hot afternoon. Cold drinks sit on the counter while the barista waits.

turns.speaker: Barista
turns.text: Welcome back! What would you like today?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: I want something cold. What fruit teas do you have?

turns.speaker: Barista
turns.text: We have peach tea and mango tea. Both are cold and sweet.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: I will have the mango tea, please. No sugar, please.

blocks.title: Your Turn: Order Your Favourite Drink

items.prompt: Imagine you are at a cafe. What drink do you want? How do you order it? Practise saying your order out loud. Use at least two phrases from the lesson.
items.answer: Open answer. For example: I would like a large iced mango tea, please. No sugar. For here.
items.explanation: Try to include the drink name, the size, and one extra detail such as milk type or sugar preference.

items.prompt: Cafes offer hot drinks like lattes and cappuccinos, and cold drinks like iced teas and fruit teas. Knowing how to ask about size, milk, and sugar makes ordering much easier. Which type of cafe drink do you like most, and why?
items.answer: Open answer. For example: I like iced mango tea because it is sweet and refreshing on a hot day.
items.explanation: There is no wrong answer. The goal is to use the vocabulary you have learned.

items.prompt: What phrase would you use to ask for a drink without sugar?
items.explanation: This short phrase is polite and easy to remember.

rows.meaning: A small, strong coffee made by pushing hot water through ground coffee beans.
rows.example: An espresso is the base for many cafe drinks.

rows.meaning: A coffee drink made with espresso and lots of steamed milk.
rows.example: A latte has a mild, creamy taste.

rows.meaning: A coffee drink like a latte but with a thick layer of foam on top.
rows.example: She ordered a cappuccino with extra foam.

rows.meaning: A person who works at a cafe and makes coffee and other drinks.
rows.example: The barista made a beautiful latte.
